notes: EBIT is proxied as Operating Income (Income Statement line item in the SEC 'Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (Loss)'). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
D&A uses 'Depreciation and amortization expenses' from the statement of comprehensive income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Capex uses 'Purchases of property and equipment' from the statement of cash flows (converted to absolute dollars). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

NWC construction: NWC = (Total current assets - Cash and cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - Current portion of long-term debt). Reported as negative because customer deposits drive current liabilities higher than operating current assets. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Tax rate: FY-effective tax expense is negative in the latest years; base-case tax_rate is normalized to 0.02. This is a modeling assumption rather than an exact effective rate observation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
WACC and terminal growth are not explicitly disclosed by the company; they are modeled assumptions for the DCF package (base 0.09, terminal growth 0.02).

NOL balance: the 10-K discusses gross deferred tax assets primarily relating to NOLs of approximately $25M; this is used as a proxy for nol_balance in this input package. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Comparable multiples: EV/EBITDA and forward P/E are taken from publicly available proxy sites; EV/NTM Revenue and strict EV/NTM EBITDA are not consistently available in retrieved sources, so those fields are set to null where not retrievable.

catalysts: Ship delivery and ramp execution (including new ship on-order/capacity pipeline) that sustains higher net yields and occupancy. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
Operating leverage if demand remains resilient while fixed costs and marketing scale with capacity.
Capital markets actions (debt refinancing and return of capital) that change interest expense and free cash flow.
company_overview: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. operates global cruise itineraries across multiple regions, with 2025 revenue of $17.935B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Operating income (used as EBIT proxy) reached $4.910B in 2025, expanding from $2.878B in 2023 as utilization and pricing normalized. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

The business is depreciation-intensive (2025 D&A: $1.718B) and requires sustained capital investment around ship deliveries and modernization. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 performance: total revenues $17.935B and operating income $4.910B; provision for income taxes was $(82)M. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
2026 capital expenditures are guided to approximately $5B (based on existing ships on order). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Balance sheet snapshot at FY2025 year-end: cash & cash equivalents $0.825B and interest-bearing debt (current + long-term) of $21.345B; noncontrolling interest $0.208B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth (2026-2030) after the strong 2023-2025 recovery phase. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin modeled to gradually improve toward ~0.28 by 2030, consistent with the historical move from 2023 (0.207) to 2025 (0.274). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Reinvestment discipline modeled via capex intensity tapering from the elevated 2025 delivery year toward a normalized run-rate, while still reflecting the 2026 capex guide. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))

Working capital is structurally negative (customer deposits), so NWC is held around ~-0.42 of sales in the model, supporting cash conversion under steady demand. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Demand/yield compression from macro shocks, geopolitical disruptions, or changes in consumer travel preferences.
Cost volatility (fuel and foreign exchange) and hedge effectiveness reducing EBIT margins relative to the base case.
High leverage increases downside sensitivity to refinancing/interest-rate risk.

valuation_summary: The DCF uses an exit-multiple terminal framework (EV/EBITDA) with terminal growth consistent with mature developed-economy long-run expectations. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nclh/statistics/?utm_source=openai))

Comparable-company spot checks are based on forward P/E and EV/EBITDA proxies from public sources for cruise peers (e.g., NCLH and TUI), used to sanity-check terminal multiple selection. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nclh/statistics/?utm_source=openai))

Net adjustments use FY2025 cash, debt, and noncontrolling interest from the latest annual report to align the equity value bridge with the historical balance-sheet base. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/884887/000088488726000007/rcl-20251231.htm))
